correctness.rationale: The degree/forest identity \(2k=9+e(S)+c(P-S)\) proves \(k\ge5\) and shows equality forces independent five-sets with induced tree complements. Exactly \(\binom{18}{5}=8568\) candidates are independently exhausted in LCF and incidence encodings, with disjoint-set union versus leaf peeling. Both reconstruct identical 252 exact solution masks, 630 swaps, full component lists, 216-core distance distributions, and a subgroup of 216 automorphisms. The packaged complete state/edge certificate was replayed. No claim about larger graphs is made.

originality.rationale: The novelty assessment concerns the fully specified \(252\)-state one-vertex exchange graph, its \(216+6\times6\) decomposition, pure/mixed-side dichotomy, and exact core metric. Earlier general cubic decycling bounds/structure and reconfiguration existence examples do not imply these enumerative and metric details. Both accessible original preprints were inspected by relevant sections and text searches; the 2023 publisher reconfiguration work has only material from indexed primary text, not a full copy. Publication-priority uncertainty is recorded rather than treated as proof of uniqueness.

value.rationale: The optimal-feedback-vertex-set exchange graph is a motivated reachability object for subcubic graphs, particularly because published results distinguish connectivity of nonminimum versus minimum states. In a canonical arc-transitive cubic incidence graph, all 252 optimum states and their reachability geometry naturally split into six pure-side K6 islands and a mixed-side 216-vertex core with distinct eccentricity classes. This is a complete structural finite classification and meaningful sharp metric benchmark, not simply a minimum-cardinality or known-table restatement.
